seoTitle: Buy a GoDaddy Domain and Email Starter Bundle
metaDescription: Get a professional domain and branded email together with GoDaddy's Email Starter bundle. Learn how to register, choose the plan, and set up your inbox.
intro: A domain with no matching email address looks unfinished — customers still expect to see you@yourbusiness.com rather than a free webmail address in your signature. GoDaddy bundles a domain registration with a Professional Email plan so both pieces get set up in the same checkout instead of two separate purchases. This guide follows the real flow: signing into your account, searching for the domain, adding the email plan, and getting your inbox usable afterward.

steps.heading: Sign in to your GoDaddy account
steps.body: Start at GoDaddy's sign-in page and log in with your username or customer number and password, or use Google, Facebook, or Apple if you've linked one of those. If you're brand new to GoDaddy, use the "Create an Account" link instead — you'll need an account either way before a domain or email plan can be attached to it. Keeping "Keep me signed in" checked saves you re-logging in every time you come back to finish setup.

image.caption: GoDaddy's sign-in screen. Existing customers log in with their username or customer number; new users create an account from the same page.

steps.heading: Search for and register your domain
steps.body: Once you're in, the account home screen puts a domain search bar front and center — type the name you want and GoDaddy checks availability across extensions, starting with the promoted .com pricing shown right on the dashboard. Pick a name that's short, easy to say out loud, and close to your business name, since this is what becomes both your website address and the second half of your email address. Add it to your cart and register it before moving on to the email plan.

image.caption: The GoDaddy account dashboard, with the domain search bar and a promoted first-year .com price front and center.

steps.heading: Add the Professional Email plan to your order
steps.body: Scroll to the "More ways to grow" section on the same dashboard and you'll see Professional Email listed as its own card, separate from hosting or additional domain extensions. It's billed per user per month, includes a set amount of storage per mailbox, and is pitched specifically on building trust — an email address that matches your domain reads as more credible than a generic free-provider address. Add it alongside your domain purchase so both come through the same checkout and renewal cycle.

image.caption: The Professional Email card on the GoDaddy dashboard, shown with its per-user monthly price and storage details.

steps.heading: Review pricing and billing terms before checkout
steps.body: Before you confirm the order, check whether the price shown is a first-year or first-term promotional rate, since domain and email renewals commonly jump to a higher rate afterward. Note the billing cycle too — email plans are typically monthly or annual per mailbox, while the domain renews yearly on its own separate date. Reading this now avoids a surprise on your card statement a year in.

steps.heading: Activate and configure your new mailbox
steps.body: After checkout, GoDaddy walks you through activating the email account, which means choosing your actual address (the part before the @ sign), setting a password, and confirming the domain it's tied to. This step is what actually turns the purchase into a working inbox — buying the plan alone doesn't create the mailbox until you complete activation.

steps.heading: Connect your inbox to webmail, Gmail, or Outlook
steps.body: Once active, you can check mail directly through GoDaddy's webmail interface, or connect the account to Gmail or Outlook using the IMAP settings GoDaddy provides so you can read and send from an app you already use daily. Connecting it to an existing client is worth doing if you don't want to remember to check a separate webmail login — most people end up routing GoDaddy mail into whatever inbox they already live in.

faq.question: Is the Email Starter plan cheaper than buying email separately?
faq.answer: Bundling email with a domain purchase through the same checkout is generally more cost-effective than buying the domain and a mailbox plan as two separate transactions later.

faq.question: Can I connect my GoDaddy email to Gmail or Outlook?
faq.answer: Yes, GoDaddy email can be accessed through Gmail or Outlook using the IMAP details GoDaddy provides, in addition to its own webmail interface.

faq.question: How many email addresses come with the Starter plan?
faq.answer: Professional Email is priced per user per month, so you choose how many mailboxes you need — start with one and add more as your team grows.

faq.question: Do I need to already own a domain to get the bundle?
faq.answer: No. The dashboard flow is built to let you search for and register a brand-new domain and attach the email plan to it in the same session.

faq.question: What happens to the price after the first year?
faq.answer: Both the domain and the email plan typically renew at a higher standard rate after the introductory term, so check the renewal price shown at checkout before confirming.
